newsitem.title: USA: Ohio poll shows Clinton lead down to two points.
newsitem.headline: Ohio poll shows Clinton lead down to two points.

text.p: In a University of Cincinnati tracking poll released on Election Day morning, President Bill Clinton's lead over Bob Dole in Ohio narrowed to just two points, making the race for the key battleground state too close to call, the university said on Tuesday.

"Following more than a year in which President Clinton has held commanding leads over Senator Dole, the race has come down to the final day as a statistical 'dead heat,'" the university said in a news release.
Clinton's lead was 13 points in a poll the university released last Wednesday. On Saturday the university said it had dropped to six points.

Ohio, with 21 electoral votes, is a key state that has voted on the winning side in all but two presidential contests this century. No Republican has ever been elected president without carrying the state.

Asked by phone whom they planned to vote for, 46 percent of likely voters in the latest poll said Clinton and 44 percent said Dole, the university said. Nine percent said they planned to vote for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, a one-point gain from last week.

The poll included 1,059 likely voters interviewed Thursday through Monday and had an error margin of plus or minus 3.0 points. It was sponsored by the university, the Cincinnati Enquirer newspaper and WLWT television.
